text:
A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a Congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.
Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions. They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration.
Should recipients agree, the voluntary interviews could commence as soon as next week. They would be likely to take place under the whistleblower protection act or the victim and witness protection act, although the potential interviewees will seek legal advice before agreeing to take part.
The investigation’s gathering of momentum will increase pressure on Infantino, who could be among those subpoenaed to give evidence to the committee in January. The committee is controlled by Democrats after their success in the midterms and is likely to be chaired by Jamie Raskin, who warned in July that it would “have the tools we need to get answers, expose corruption, protect sports fans against exorbitant and fraudulent charges and block this attempt to turn world soccer into a global financial shakedown”.
The White House has previously dismissed similar allegations as politically motivated. Fifa did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Subpoenas could be issued to a range of individuals within Fifa, and in the organisation’s orbit, as soon as the second week of January. Those required to give evidence at a hearing could be required to disclose their knowledge of the FFE plan and other Fifa controversies, potentially handing over physical evidence.
Fifa confirmed on Thursday it had fallen victim to a criminal cyberattack carried out by a group that posed as staff members to steal personal and business data. A group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claimed responsibility for the breach, understood to have taken place on 11 November.
In a letter to the Fifa council dated 25 November, seen by the Guardian, the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, said the hack had “resulted in information being illegally obtained which included data relevant to the personal profiles of key officials including Fifa Council members attending Fifa tournaments and events”. Grafström wrote that Fifa had “taken mitigating and corrective steps” and told council members that they would be contacted individually where necessary.
digest_he: מספר עובדים בהווה ובעבר בפיפ"א קיבלו בקשות לקיים ראיונות עדות במסגרת חקירה שמנהלת ועדת המשפטים של בית הנבחרים האמריקאי, בהובלת דמוקרטים. החקירה מתמקדת בבדיקת תוכנית פרויקט שנכשלה ובקשרים בין הארגון לבין ממשל טראמפ. במקביל, פיפ"א אישרה כי נפלה קורבן למתקפת סייבר עבריינית מצד קבוצת האקרים שהתחזתה לאנשי צוות וגנבה נתונים אישיים ועסקיים רגישים של בכירים בארגון.
